description: S-box lookup tables: table[x] = S(x) for input integer x (S(0) = table[0]). Bit-order conventions are in each entry's notes. Built and cross-checked 2026-11-13; verified_against lists the independent sources each table was compared with programmatically.

sboxes.name: present
sboxes.source: Bogdanov et al., PRESENT: An Ultra-Lightweight Block Cipher, CHES 2007, Sect. 3 (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-74735-2_31)
verified_against: Sovyn, Opirskyy, Mykhaylova, CEUR-WS Vol-3504 paper 3 (2023), Table 7 (https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3504/paper3.pdf)
Wei, Sun, Liu, Hu, Zhang, IACR CiC 1(4) 2024, Table 2 (https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/20)
sboxes.notes: Also the S-box of LED (CHES 2011, https://eprint.iacr.org/2012/600) and PHOTON. Spec writes the 4-bit input as (x3,x2,x1,x0) with x0 = LSB; table[x] uses the integer value x.

sboxes.name: led
sboxes.source: Guo, Peyrin, Poschmann, Robshaw, The LED Block Cipher, CHES 2011 (https://eprint.iacr.org/2012/600): uses the PRESENT S-box
sboxes.notes: Alias: identical table to 'present'.

sboxes.name: gift
sboxes.source: Banik et al., GIFT: A Small Present, CHES 2017 (https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/622); GIFT-COFB NIST LWC round-2 spec Sect. 2 (https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/lightweight-cryptography/documents/round-2/spec-doc-rnd2/gift-cofb-spec-round2.pdf)
verified_against: Sovyn, Opirskyy, Mykhaylova, CEUR-WS Vol-3504 paper 3 (2023), Table 7 (https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3504/paper3.pdf)
Wei, Sun, Liu, Hu, Zhang, IACR CiC 1(4) 2024, Table 2 (https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/20)
sboxes.notes: GS. Recomputed from the GIFT-COFB bitsliced SubCells sequence with S0 = bit 0 (LSB). Spec writes the 4-bit input as (x3,x2,x1,x0) with x0 = LSB; table[x] uses the integer value x.

sboxes.name: skinny64
sboxes.source: Beierle et al., The SKINNY Family of Block Ciphers, CRYPTO 2016 (https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/660), S4
verified_against: Sovyn, Opirskyy, Mykhaylova, CEUR-WS Vol-3504 paper 3 (2023), Table 7 (https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3504/paper3.pdf)
Wei, Sun, Liu, Hu, Zhang, IACR CiC 1(4) 2024, Table 2 (https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/20)
sboxes.notes: Recomputed from the bit-level definition: x0 ^= NOR(x3,x2), then rotate (x3,x2,x1,x0)->(x2,x1,x0,x3); 4 times, no rotation after the last; x0 = LSB.

sboxes.source: Borghoff et al., PRINCE, ASIACRYPT 2012 (https://eprint.iacr.org/2012/529), S-layer
verified_against: Sovyn, Opirskyy, Mykhaylova, CEUR-WS Vol-3504 paper 3 (2023), Table 7 (https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3504/paper3.pdf)
sboxes.notes: Spec writes the 4-bit input as (x3,x2,x1,x0) with x0 = LSB; table[x] uses the integer value x.

verified_against: Sovyn, Opirskyy, Mykhaylova, CEUR-WS Vol-3504 paper 3 (2023), Table 7 (https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3504/paper3.pdf)

sboxes.notes: Involution. Same S-box as MANTIS and CRAFT (per SageMath). Used by Midori64. Spec writes the 4-bit input as (x3,x2,x1,x0) with x0 = LSB; table[x] uses the integer value x.

sboxes.name: noekeon
sboxes.source: Daemen, Peeters, Van Assche, Rijmen, Nessie Proposal: NOEKEON, 2000 (https://gro.noekeon.org/), Gamma
verified_against: Sovyn, Opirskyy, Mykhaylova, CEUR-WS Vol-3504 paper 3 (2023), Table 7 (https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3504/paper3.pdf)
sboxes.notes: Involution. Gamma is specified as a bitsliced map on four 32-bit words; this is its 4-bit S-box view as listed by SageMath and Sovyn et al. Not re-derived from the Noekeon document (bit-to-word assignment unverified).

sboxes.name: pride
sboxes.source: Albrecht et al., Block Ciphers - Focus on the Linear Layer (feat. PRIDE), CRYPTO 2014 (https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/453)

sboxes.notes: Involution. Same table as the Prost (CAESAR) S-box. Spec writes the 4-bit input as (x3,x2,x1,x0) with x0 = LSB; table[x] uses the integer value x.

sboxes.name: printcipher
sboxes.source: Knudsen, Leander, Poschmann, Robshaw, PRINTcipher, CHES 2010 (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-15031-9_2)
verified_against: Wei, Sun, Liu, Hu, Zhang, IACR CiC 1(4) 2024, Table 2 (https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/20)
sboxes.notes: Base 3-bit S-box. PRINTcipher applies key-dependent permutations of the 3 input bits before it; this is the fixed table as in SageMath and Wei et al.; not re-read from the PRINTcipher paper.

sboxes.name: chi3
sboxes.source: Definition: chi map (as in Keccak) on 3 bits
sboxes.notes: COMPUTED, not transcribed. 'table' uses a_0 = MSB of the index (bit 2), i.e. your x0 = a_0, and b_0 = MSB of the output. With a_0 = LSB the table is table_a0_lsb.

sboxes.name: ascon
sboxes.source: NIST SP 800-232 (Aug 2025), Sect. 3.3, Table 6 and Eq. (7) (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-232); Ascon v1.2 round-2 spec Table 5 (https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/lightweight-cryptography/documents/round-2/spec-doc-rnd2/ascon-spec-round2.pdf)
sboxes.notes: x0 is the MSB and x4 the LSB of the index (SP 800-232: x=1 is (x0..x4)=(0,0,0,0,1)); output y0 = MSB. Matches your x0/y0 = MSB convention directly.

sboxes.name: keccak_chi5
sboxes.source: Bertoni, Daemen, Peeters, Van Assche, The Keccak reference 3.0, chi step (https://keccak.team/files/Keccak-reference-3.0.pdf)
sboxes.notes: COMPUTED from the definition. 'table' uses a_0 = MSB of the index (your x0 = a_0) and equals Stoffelen's 'keccak' table. With a_0 = LSB (lane x = bit x) the table is table_a0_lsb; the two differ by bit reversal of input and output.

sboxes.name: skinny128
sboxes.source: SKINNY-AEAD/SKINNY-Hash NIST LWC round-2 spec, Appendix A (https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/lightweight-cryptography/documents/round-2/spec-doc-rnd2/SKINNY-spec-round2.pdf); Beierle et al., CRYPTO 2016 (https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/660)
sboxes.notes: S8; x0 = LSB in the spec. Recomputed from the definition (x4 ^= NOR(x7,x6), x0 ^= NOR(x3,x2), then (x7..x0)->(x2,x1,x7,x6,x4,x0,x3,x5); four rounds, the last only swaps x1 and x2).

sboxes.name: aes
sboxes.source: FIPS 197 (upd1, 2023), Sect. 5.1.1, Table 4 (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.197-upd1)
sboxes.notes: Computed as affine(inverse in GF(2^8) mod x^8+x^4+x^3+x+1), constant 0x63; equals FIPS 197 Table 4. FIPS bit b0 = LSB, b7 = MSB, so your x0 = b7.

sboxes.name: sm4
sboxes.source: GB/T 32907-2016 (SM4); table as in SageMath 'SMS4'; see also https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ribose-cfrg-sm4/
sboxes.notes: One transcribed source (SageMath). Independently consistent: all 256 entries equal A*inv(A*x + 0xD3) + 0xD3 with inversion mod x^8+x^7+x^6+x^5+x^4+x^2+1 and A circulant with first row 0xD3 (found by our own search). Not checked against GB/T 32907 itself.

sboxes.name: camellia_s1
sboxes.source: RFC 3713, Camellia, SBOX1 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3713)
sboxes.notes: RFC 3713 and SageMath 'Camellia' transcriptions agree; permutation. Not re-derived algebraically. SBOX2(x)=SBOX1(x)<<<1, SBOX3(x)=SBOX1(x)<<<7, SBOX4(x)=SBOX1(x<<<1).
